cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and the work is coloured by what you already carry.
cells.act: go where the feeling is already pulling
cells.ask: Today, follow whatever piece of the work already feels warm — a single page, not the whole plan — and let the sitting start there.
cells.core: The direction comes through the practising rather than being argued into it. At the bench, only the next step shows, and that is plenty for one session; the repetitions stop feeling like drudgery because each one walks toward something already lighting the dark out front. Experience lands first, and the images come after — which is why the ideas move you instead of running you.
cells.sheetLine: Your work points somewhere, and that somewhere is yours.
cells.verb: moving through uncertainty without forcing it to be clear
cells.place: in the small repeated practice you keep alone

cells.tense: The dream is running ahead of the practice, and next week's version of it is doing the work instead of you.
cells.act: tend it small and ask nothing of it
cells.ask: Make today's sitting smaller than seems serious, keep it, and ask no result of it — no sign, no progress — just that one session, tended.
cells.core: The imagining has run past what the hands can do. Whole outcomes are visible before any session has been set down, and the visible version is doing the work in your head while the real repetitions wait. The glow is real; it's just arrived before the practice it was supposed to serve. The planning feels lit, and each session has started to look small next to it.
cells.sheetLine: The glow has run out past the practice.

cells.tense: The practice has gone flat over the door you're still standing at.
cells.act: notice what you already know before you reason about it
cells.ask: Before today's sitting, put down the first thing that came to you about the piece, three lines at most, before any reasons. Then begin as usual.
cells.core: The practice runs on what can be checked. The step under you has to be solid before you take it, and ambiguity gets answered with a plain no or a worn-out shrug. The repetitions are still there, moving through the hands with nothing symbolic in them — no reason for them that isn't already proven. Anything that arrives without evidence gets turned away at the door.
cells.sheetLine: You still practise, but nothing unproven is allowed near it.

cells.tense: The pen is down in a room where you are already writing, and the practice is carrying more than you'd say.
cells.act: keep the session even when it feels pointless
cells.ask: Keep each sitting as it is this week, even the pointless ones, and some evening, on a plain page, name what you actually want from the work. Then close the notebook.
cells.core: By the shrug in the answer, the planning is already doing things you don't claim. A drawing comes before you'd say you're an artist, a routine gets defended as just a habit. Something is shaping where you point the practice, and you'd rather it didn't have that much say. Keeping it out of the record doesn't keep it out of your hands.
cells.sheetLine: You're steering by something you would not put on paper.
